correctness.rationale: For each new vertex the lower/upper sets in the chain are uniquely determined by 0<=l_i<=u_i<=n. Comparability among new points forces both cuts isotone; incomparability forbids the two possible chain witnesses, exactly l_i<=u_j and l_j<=u_i. These inequalities are necessary and sufficient for a valid induced extension by transitivity/path contraction. Each labelled new-point poset F yields an endpoint poset Q_F of 2r vertices with no directed cycles; finite homogeneous extension identifies these with complete types. Decomposition by image size yields T_r(n)=sum_F sum_k SurjIso(Q_F,[k])*binom(n+1,k). Every Q_F admits a linear extension, so k=2r coefficient positive and degree exactly 2r. The 2- and 3-point formulas and orientations agree with a standalone checker independent of endpoint enumeration in 15 exhaustive small direct-extension instances, including r=3,n=3. Computational checks are explicitly finite and not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: A nontrivial parameter-sensitive orbit-counting invariant in a homogeneous model is reduced uniformly, for every fixed tuple arity, to standard finite order-polynomial data through a newly specified 2r-endpoint constraint poset. This yields a natural full-arity polynomial-versus-exponential contrast between chain and antichain parameter structures; positive integer binomial coefficients; sharp 2r degree; exact arity-two and arity-three formulas; and a structural derivation of a 1/4:1/4:1/2 limiting relation distribution. These are mathematically motivated structural results, not an arbitrary table slice or solely a sequence lookup.
